The proposed ISAC system uses movable antennas capable of sub-wavelength positioning within a predefined 2D spatial area.
A two-timescale optimization framework adjusts antenna positions once per scanning period and beamforming vectors plus snapshot durations every snapshot.
The system divides the scanning sector into Q slices, each illuminated sequentially by directional beams during snapshots.
The optimization problem is a mixed integer nonlinear program (MINLP) involving discrete antenna positions and continuous beamforming variables.
Imperfect CSI is modeled with a bounded uncertainty set, capturing estimation errors and outdated channel information.
Dynamic RCS fluctuations are modeled using radar Swerling models, introducing chance constraints for sensing QoS.
Minimum distance constraints between antennas ensure physical feasibility and avoid mutual coupling.
Beamforming vectors are optimized to match ideal directional beam patterns with low sidelobe leakage for accurate sensing.
The system transmits both communication signals to K single-antenna users and dedicated radar sensing signals simultaneously.
The channel model includes Rician fading with LoS and NLoS components dependent on antenna positions.
Mechanical repositioning of antennas typically takes milliseconds, making frequent repositioning impractical.
The proposed AO-based algorithm efficiently finds high-quality suboptimal solutions to the complex optimization problem.
Simulation results indicate significant transmit power reduction compared to fixed-position antenna systems.
The TTS framework achieves similar performance to systems repositioning antennas every snapshot but with much less repositioning overhead.
The DFRC base station does not assume prior knowledge of target locations, treating all sector entities as potential targets.
Snapshot durations are optimized to adapt sensing and communication time allocation dynamically.
The system uses a uniform field response vector (FRV) to model the multipath channel components.
The transmit signal covariance matrix includes contributions from communication beamforming and radar sensing signals.
The antenna positions are selected from a finite set of discrete candidate positions determined by actuator precision.
The sensing SINR is affected by both beamforming design and dynamic RCS fluctuations.
